findings.claim: Unit mass recovery is a compact measured-data screening control across these flask conditions, but it is not universally stoichiometric or an industrial replacement for GA assay.
findings.falsification: A development-worse flexible model is more accurate on the single exposed heldout condition; no optimality claim.
findings.scope: Contemporaneous HPLC diagnostic; condition transfer is retrospective.
findings.known_prior_art: The authors already report acetate-enhanced EG assimilation and GA production with isotope evidence. Mass-ratio stoichiometry is a comparator, not a discovery. We test predictive recovery heterogeneity without asserting causal pH effects.

findings.claim: pH-only recovery, product-loss time trend, medium coefficients, saturation and acid-dissociation gates do not improve whole-condition development transfer.
findings.falsification: pH and feed identity are confounded; the time term has the wrong sign for loss; saturation plateau reaches its upper bound.
findings.scope: Failure of these tested low-dimensional mechanisms, not disproof of biological pH effects.
findings.known_prior_art: The authors already report acetate-enhanced EG assimilation and GA production with isotope evidence. Mass-ratio stoichiometry is a comparator, not a discovery. We test predictive recovery heterogeneity without asserting causal pH effects.
findings.underlying_proposal_disposition: unsupported: the tested extensions did not improve the prespecified development comparison
